CUDA toolkit (nvcc, cudart, cuDNN, onnxruntime) stitched into the canonical /usr layout on Fedora and Arch
Installs the CUDA compiler driver (nvcc), the CUDA runtime/dev
libraries (cudart, nvrtc, cupti, curand, cccl, cufile), cuDNN, and
onnxruntime. On Fedora the RPMs land in /usr directly; on Arch the
post-install tasks symlink the /opt/cuda binaries, headers, and libs
into the same /usr-rooted paths, so every downstream GPU consumer
compiles against one layout regardless of distro. Each artifact is a
real file or library on disk, so its presence is directly verifiable.

## Acceptance plan

This candy's `plan:` — the runnable spec `charly check` executes against a live deployment. `check:` steps are idempotent probes; `run:` steps change state.

| Intent | Step |
|---|---|
| `run` | command=if [ ! -f /etc/fedora-release ]; then exit 0 fi CUDNN_DIR=$(mktemp -d) cd "$CUDNN_DIR" if dnf5 download --enable-repo="fedora-multimedia" cuda-cudnn-devel 2>/dev/null; then rpm2cpio cuda-cudnn-devel*.rpm \| cpio -idm 2>/dev/null [ -d ./usr/include ] && cp -v ./usr/include/cudnn*.h /usr/include/ while IFS= read -r -d '' link; do name=$(basename "$link") versioned="" for v in /usr/lib64/"${name}".*; do if [ -f "$v" ] && ! echo "$v" \| grep -q '\.so$'; then versioned="$v"; break fi done [ -n "$versioned" ] && [ ! -e /usr/lib64/"$name" ] && ln -sv "$(basename "$versioned")" /usr/lib64/"$name" done < <(find ./usr/lib64 -maxdepth 1 -name '*.so' -type l -print0 2>/dev/null) fi cd / && rm -rf "$CUDNN_DIR" |
| `run` | command=if [ ! -f /etc/arch-release ]; then exit 0 fi # nvcc + cuobjdump + ptxas + nvprof — every binary in /opt/cuda/bin for bin in /opt/cuda/bin/*; do [ -e "$bin" ] && ln -sf "$bin" /usr/bin/$(basename "$bin") done # Headers — cudnn*.h live in /opt/cuda/targets/x86_64-linux/include # on the cudnn package, while CUDA's own headers live in # /opt/cuda/include. Symlink both into /usr/include. # Headers — link EVERY ENTRY of each toolkit include root, not a guessed subset. # nvcc computes its default include root RELATIVE to its own executable, and # /usr/bin/nvcc is a symlink, so all CUDA headers must be reachable under # /usr/include. Enumerating by pattern is what broke this: a `*.h` glob linked the # top-level headers but silently dropped (a) the SUBTREES crt/ and cccl/, which # killed every build at CMake's enable_language(CUDA) with "crt/host_config.h: No # such file or directory", and then (b) the `.hpp` half of the `_functions` family # (`vector_functions.hpp` and friends), which killed the very next stage -- both # reported on opencharly/layer-cuda#9. Linking every entry needs no extension list # to keep in sync and cannot silently miss a file or a subtree again. # nvcc resolves its OWN helpers relative to its own executable path. Through the # /usr/bin/nvcc symlink that means /usr/<sibling>/ — so the toolkit's sibling TREES # must exist at /usr too, not only its files. Without /usr/nvvm, nvcc cannot find its # backend compiler at all: "$CICC_PATH/cicc: No such file or directory" # (/usr/sbin/../nvvm/bin/cicc), and every CUDA compile dies while PREPROCESSING # still succeeds — which is exactly how the check added in #10 stayed green through # it. Both halves of that lesson are fixed here. for tree in nvvm; do [ -d "/opt/cuda/$tree" ] && [ ! -e "/usr/$tree" ] && ln -sfn "/opt/cuda/$tree" "/usr/$tree" done for root in /opt/cuda/include /opt/cuda/targets/x86_64-linux/include; do [ -d "$root" ] \|\| continue for entry in "$root"/*; do [ -e "$entry" ] \|\| continue ln -sfn "$entry" /usr/include/"$(basename "$entry")" done done # Libraries: libcudart, libcudnn, libcurand, etc. mkdir -p /usr/lib64 # Enumerate EVERY entry, not a `*.so*` glob. nvcc links the STATIC archives by # default (libcudart_static.a, libcudadevrt.a, libculibos.a, ...), and a `.so*` # pattern cannot match a `.a` — so the linker failed with "cannot find # -lcudart_static: No such file or directory" although the package ships the file # (opencharly/layer-cuda#12). Same defect shape as the `*.h` header glob that missed # `.hpp`: pattern-matching a directory instead of enumerating it. mkdir -p /usr/lib64 for libdir in /opt/cuda/targets/x86_64-linux/lib /opt/cuda/lib64; do [ -d "$libdir" ] \|\| continue for entry in "$libdir"/*; do [ -e "$entry" ] \|\| continue ln -sfn "$entry" /usr/lib64/"$(basename "$entry")" done done |
